why_this_works: Seeding the Romas removes excess water so you get a thick, chunky salsa instead of soup. The lime juice and hot sauce hit both acid and heat, which brightens the raw tomatoes and keeps the cilantro from tasting soapy to borderline tasters. Pulsing in the food processor rather than hand-chopping gives you an even texture fast while still leaving enough body.

steps: Seed and chop the Roma tomatoes.
Roughly chop the cilantro and green onions.
Combine tomatoes, jalapeños, cilantro, and green onions in a food processor or blender.
Mix in hot sauce, garlic powder, salt, pepper, and lime juice.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Chill before serving for best flavor.
